anomalies.observed: C6 is a Device:C unpolarized capacitor, value 0.1uF, but its footprint is Inductor_SMD:L_0805_2012Metric_Pad1.05x1.20mm_HandSolder. Pin 1 sits alone on the auto-named net unconnected-(C6-Pad1), so the part is electrically dangling; only pin 2 reaches GND.
anomalies.expected: A 0.1uF capacitor should carry a capacitor footprint and be connected across the rail it is meant to decouple. Nothing in the specification calls for a dangling inductor-footprint capacitor.
anomalies.impact: The part has no effect on the circuit as wired. If it was meant to decouple a rail, that decoupling is missing, and the footprint would be wrong for a capacitor assembly.

anomalies.observed: In the negative-side diode chain of the EPD charge pump, U10 has its anode (pin 2) on Net-(U10-A) and its cathode (pin 1) on GND. This is the reverse of the GND-to-node orientation a negative charge pump normally uses, so the chain may not pump the negative rail as intended. The orientation cannot be confirmed from the netlist alone.
anomalies.expected: In the negative multiplier, the first rectifier should conduct from GND into the pump node, so its anode should be on GND and its cathode on the pump node, matching the Pervasive Displays reference rectifier arrangement.

evidence.quote: EPD charge-pump/multiplier rectifiers | U1/U2/U3 = SS2040FL ×3 | Exact part, exact quantity

anomalies.impact: If the orientation is reversed, the negative display rail (VGL-type supply) may not be generated, and the EPD panel would not refresh correctly.

parsed.summary: The power section, battery path, EPD boost and charge-pump component values, and the keyboard and SD pin assignments all match the specification. The most concrete deviation is the dangling 0.1uF capacitor C6 with an inductor footprint, and the negative charge-pump diode orientation is a lower-confidence concern, so the overall verdict is weak.
